svg.aria-label: Branches of optical computing — time × what is computed
svg.text: Branches of optical computing — time × what is computed
Horizontal = year (stretched after 2010) · rows = what is computed · dot colour = where light flows. History and taxonomy on one sheet
What Miller 2010 covered — digital logic, and its lesson (light wins at connecting)
Analog computing — Miller's logic-device yardstick does not apply directly (precision and noise matter instead of level restoration)
1976 · Gibbs et al. first demo (1985 book) — fails most criteria
S-SEED · the only one to pass
1960 · Cutrona et al. · radar imaging (matched filter Vander Lugt 1964)

How to read — Miller 2010 asks what it takes to be a logic device, so it fits the top two rows. The four rows below (analog computing) date back to the 1960s but grew sharply after 2010 with integrated photonics and AI demand.

A third axis (where light meets electronics — all-optical / O-E-O / electronic compute + optical I/O) is mixed point by point, so it is left out. Results that bridge rows, like reservoir equalization (2025), are where new work appears.
